entities.summary: Yoriko Kawaguchi  is a Japanese politician and former economist, who served as a Japanese Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2002 to 2004 and continued as a special advisor to then-Japanese Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi for foreign affairs from 2004 to 2005. A member of Liberal Democratic Party, she previously served as a Japanese Minister of the Environment from 2000 to 2002. She was also a member of the House of Councillors for Liberal Democratic Party from 2005 to 2013. In July 2008, she was appointed co-chair of a new International Commission on Nuclear Non-proliferation and Disarmament, with former Australian Foreign Minister Gareth Evans.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a key advisor to Japanese Prime Minister Junichiro Koizumi and co-chair of the International Commission on Nuclear Non-proliferation and Disarmament, Yoriko Kawaguchi played a significant role in shaping Japan's foreign policy and nuclear non-proliferation efforts. Her appointment in 2008 marked a notable shift in Japan's approach to nuclear disarmament.
